## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Nav bar — 11 text links (Get Started, Tutorial, Concepts, API,
  Problem, Capabilities, Results, Quick Start, Report, Paper, Writing,
  Roadmap) + 2 buttons — too many to scan; suggest ~5-6 primary links.
- Results / "What we measured" — 12 cards (under the 20 hard cap, so
  not a hard violation) — but each card's tag is a dense jargon string,
  so a stranger skims none. Suggest cutting to ~5-6 headline rows with
  plain-English tags.
- Features — effectively 7 large span-2 cards — reads long for a
  landing page. Per-card word counts are within the 120-word cap

- NOTE (accuracy): no individual bento/r-card exceeds the word caps;
  the hero r-card body is ~47 words (under 60). The bloat here is
  card-count and nav-link-count, not per-card length.

### Internal jargon
- Hero stat "382 Completed milestones" — "milestone" is an internal
  process unit; 382 of them means nothing to an outsider (and reads as
  process noise).
- Hero r-card — "Repinned from v2 0.9857," "architecture-only 0.8947,"
  "dual-condition" — version/audit narrative a stranger can't parse.
- Results cards — "FoVer," "VeriCoT," "CRANE," "HalluGuard v3,"
  "PRM-BiasBench," "SVAMP," "GSM8K," "CCTU," "EstimationVerifier,"
  "0.91 AUROC (publication gate)" — benchmark/internal names with no

- Features → Multi-step reasoning — "AND-composed"; Adversarial card —
  "k=5 ensemble."
- Preprint title — "(paper-v6)" — version number a stranger doesn't
  need.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Hero r-card "Recent progress" — "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after
  pre-submission adversarial audit" reads like a retro/changelog line,
  not landing-page copy. (No raw ".NNN" milestone IDs appear anywhere —
  the page is otherwise clean of that pattern; this and the "382
  milestones" stat are the only milestone-narrative leaks.)

### Inconsistencies
- "0.9131 AUROC ... FoVer" (hero stat, r-card, preprint) vs "0.125
  FoVer baseline" (Math reasoning card). 0.125 AUC is worse than
  chance; presented as a baseline with no explanation, it makes the
  adjacent 0.90 look cherry-picked and the headline 0.9131 look
  unstable.
- The 47+28 worked example: intro says "47 + 28 = 76"; the
  "One-word-at-a-time" card says the LLM is committed to "47 + 28 = 7";
  the next card and the code sample say "76." The stray "= 7" reads as

- Section label "What you can check" / "Seven capabilities" but two of
  the seven cards (Research operations, TTC & PREM) describe the

  contradicts contents.
- "AUROC" vs "AUC" used interchangeably across cards (0.9131 AUROC,
  0.91 AUROC, 0.90 AUC) — minor, but sloppy to a careful reader.

### Missing essentials
- What it does / install / license / maintainer are all present and
  clear (good). 
- Trust anchor is weak where it matters: the strongest credibility
  signal — independent re-computation of the headline — is buried in
  Preprint prose, not surfaced next to the numbers in Evidence. No
  third-party signal (stars, citation, external user) anywhere.
- Maintainer is only "© 2026 Ian Blenke" in the footer. Combined with
  heavy "autonomous research loop" framing, a stranger can't tell if a
  human team stands behind the numbers or the project largely runs
  itself — a bus-factor/credibility question on a verification tool.

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — a perfect 1.0, no sample
  size on the card.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — 100%, no anchor on the card.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" — "identical" is a perfect claim.
- "99.3% of wrong code flagged" — very high, on HumanEval (164).
- "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" — the implausibly weak 0.125
  baseline inflates the contrast.
- Mitigation present: the Evidence intro asserts every number is
  artifact-backed and provenance-labeled, and the headline says
  "5-seed" — but the perfect-score *cards themselves* carry no n or CI,
  so a skeptic still flags them.

- Real install command (`pip install carnot-ebm`), Apache 2.0,
